title: Exploratory Data Analysis, Missingness Auditing, and Normalization
text: Clinical datasets electronic health records (EHR) frequently exhibit complex missingness patterns, non-standard missing codes (e.g. "999", "NA", ""), extreme statistical outliers. TempleCBE package provides domain-agnostic tools streamline exploratory data analysis (EDA), quantify missingness, normalize numerical features, flag outliers cleanly.
code: library(TempleCBE) library(dplyr)

title: Exploratory Data Analysis, Missingness Auditing, and Normalization
text: SumNa() counts missing values vectors, data frames, matrices, supporting explicit missing value codes ("NA" strings empty strings):
code: library(TempleCBE)  # Sample vector with default and non-standard missing values vec <- c(12, 14, NA, 999, 18, "")  # Count standard NAs SumNa(vec) #> [1] 1  # Count NAs including custom missing codes SumNa(vec, na_list = c("999", "")) #> [1] 3

title: Nested Cross-Validation for Longitudinal Survival Models
text: clinical trial data science observational cohort modeling, evaluating survival outcomes (e.g. time--event data censoring non-adherence) requires rigorous validation prevent data leakage hyperparameter overfitting. vignette demonstrates Nested Cross-Validation (Nested CV) pipeline using TempleCBE synthetic longitudinal clinical trial dataset generated inline .
code: Nested Resampling Architecture ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ Outer Loop: 5-Fold Group Cross-Validation (Evaluates Generalization Performance)       │ │  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  │ │  │ Inner Loop: Bootstrap / Resampling Fold (Tunes Model & Cutpoint Parameters)      │  │ │  │   • Feature Selection via Factor Analysis for Mixed Data (step_famd)             │  │ │  │   • Regularized Cox Proportional Hazards Fitting                                 │  │ │  │   • Integrated Brier Score (glmnet_IBS) Evaluation                               │  │ │  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘  │ └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

title: Nested Cross-Validation for Longitudinal Survival Models
code: if (!requireNamespace("TempleCBE", quietly = TRUE)) {   devtools::load_all("..") } else {   library(TempleCBE) }  library(dplyr) library(survival) library(tidymodels) tidymodels_prefer()  set.seed(2026)

title: Nested Cross-Validation for Longitudinal Survival Models
text: simulate longitudinal clinical cohort time-varying covariates, patient IDs, start/stop interval times (tstart, tstop), binary survival status.
code: # Generate synthetic clinical survival dataset set.seed(42) n_patients <- 100 obs_per_patient <- 4  sim_data <- expand.grid(   patient_id = paste0("PT_", sprintf("%03d", 1:n_patients)),   visit = 1:obs_per_patient ) %>%   arrange(patient_id, visit) %>%   mutate(     tstart = (visit - 1) * 30,     tstop = visit * 30,     age = rep(rnorm(n_patients, mean = 58, sd = 10), each = obs_per_patient),     bmi = rep(rnorm(n_patients, mean = 27, sd = 4), each = obs_per_patient),     score_marker = rnorm(n(), mean = 0, sd = 1),     treatment = factor(rep(sample(c("Control", "Treated"), n_patients, replace = TRUE), each = obs_per_patient))   )  # Add event status with censoring sim_data <- sim_data %>%   group_by(patient_id) %>%   mutate(     prob_event = 0.05 + 0.02 * (score_marker > 0.5) + 0.01 * (age > 60),     status = as.integer(runif(n()) < prob_event)   ) %>%   ungroup()  head(sim_data) #> # A tibble: 6 × 10 #>   patient_id visit tstart tstop   age   bmi score_marker treatment prob_event #>   <fct>      <int>  <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>        <dbl> <fct>          <dbl> #> 1 PT_001         1      0    30  71.7  31.8       -2.00  Treated         0.06 #> 2 PT_001         2     30    60  71.7  31.8        0.334 Treated         0.06 #> 3 PT_001         3     60    90  71.7  31.8        1.17  Treated         0.08 #> 4 PT_001         4     90   120  71.7  31.8        2.06  Treated         0.08 #> 5 PT_002         1      0    30  52.4  31.2       -1.38  Treated         0.05 #> 6 PT_002         2     30    60  52.4  31.2       -1.15  Treated         0.05 #> # ℹ 1 more variable: status <int>

title: Nested Cross-Validation for Longitudinal Survival Models
text: Using rsample::nested_cv(), split dataset outer resampling loop (5-fold grouped patient ID) inner tuning loop (bootstrap folds):
code: # Prepare grouped nested CV structure nested_folds <- nested_cv(   sim_data,   outside = group_vfold_cv(v = 5, group = "patient_id"),   inside = group_bootstraps(times = 5, group = "patient_id") )  nested_folds #> # Nested resampling: #> #  outer: Group 5-fold cross-validation #> #  inner: Group bootstrap sampling #> # A tibble: 5 × 3 #>   splits           id        inner_resamples  #>   <list>           <chr>     <list>           #> 1 <split [320/80]> Resample1 <g_boot [5 × 2]> #> 2 <split [320/80]> Resample2 <g_boot [5 × 2]> #> 3 <split [320/80]> Resample3 <g_boot [5 × 2]> #> 4 <split [320/80]> Resample4 <g_boot [5 × 2]> #> 5 <split [320/80]> Resample5 <g_boot [5 × 2]>

what: 6. Evaluating Models with Integrated Brier Score (glmnet_IBS)
title: Nested Cross-Validation for Longitudinal Survival Models
text: evaluate model predictive performance across resamples using Integrated Brier Score metric provided TempleCBE::glmnet_IBS(): censoring_weights = "ipcw" scores one row per patient weights inverse probability remaining uncensored, patients leave study early count much patients followed end:
code: # Cox model recipe: identifier and interval columns are kept but not used as # predictors; numeric predictors are normalized inside each fold cox_rec <- recipe(   ~ age + bmi + score_marker + treatment + patient_id + tstart + tstop + status,   data = sim_data ) %>%   update_role(patient_id, tstart, tstop, status, new_role = "id variable") %>%   step_normalize(all_numeric_predictors()) %>%   step_dummy(all_nominal_predictors())  # Evaluation grid: every distinct visit interval visit_times <- distinct(sim_data, tstart, tstop)  # IBS on outer fold 1 fold_1_split <- nested_folds$splits[[1]]  ibs_result <- glmnet_IBS(   object = fold_1_split,   alpha = 1,   recipe = cox_rec,   feature_names = c("age", "bmi", "score_marker", "treatment_Treated"),   time_data = visit_times,   id_col = "patient_id",   internal_folds = 3,   cox.ties = "breslow" ) ibs_result #> # A tibble: 2 × 5 #>      IBS lambda term         estimate alpha #>    <dbl>  <dbl> <chr>           <dbl> <dbl> #> 1 0.0563 0.0178 age            0.0886     1 #> 2 0.0563 0.0178 score_marker   0.339      1 ipcw_result <- glmnet_IBS(   object = fold_1_split,   alpha = 1,   recipe = cox_rec,   feature_names = c("age", "bmi", "score_marker", "treatment_Treated"),   time_data = visit_times,   id_col = "patient_id",   internal_folds = 3,   censoring_weights = "ipcw",   cox.ties = "breslow" ) ipcw_result #> # A tibble: 1 × 5 #>      IBS lambda term         estimate alpha #>    <dbl>  <dbl> <chr>           <dbl> <dbl> #> 1 0.0194 0.0258 score_marker    0.206     1

title: Nested Cross-Validation for Longitudinal Survival Models
text: Using TempleCBE synthetic clinical dataset: - Data Leakage Prevented: Feature extraction (step_famd) tuning take place strictly within inner resample folds. - Model Evaluation Unbiased: Outer folds provide unbiased estimate generalization accuracy via Integrated Brier Scores (glmnet_IBS). - Reproducible & Anonymized: methodologies can safely published, taught, benchmarked without exposing confidential patient health data.

text: Data counting-process (start/stop) layout: one row per subject per interval, identified `id_col`, interval bounds `start_col` `stop_col` event indicator `status_col`. 1. **Preprocessing.** `recipe` prepped analysis set – rows    `start_col == 0` (subject's first interval)    `prep_on = "baseline"` – baked onto sets, normalization    learned inside fold. recipe must keep `id_col`, `start_col`,    `stop_col` `status_col` output (e.g. `"id variable"` roles). 2. **Fit.** `cv.glmnet(family = "cox")` baked `feature_names`    (optionally narrowed `formula`), choosing `lambda.min`    `type.measure` `internal_folds` folds. 3. **Predicted survival.** \(S(t \mid x) = \exp(-H_0(t) \cdot RR)\),    \(H_0\) cumulative baseline hazard null Cox model fit    analysis set, linearly interpolated onto stop times    `time_data`, \(RR\) relative risk implied model's    linear predictor assessment set. grid times subject    interval, status carried forward \(RR\) filled    subject's last known value. 4. **Scoring** [yardstick::brier_survival_integrated()],    `censoring_weights`:    * `"none"`: every assessment interval row scored      `Surv(start, stop, status)` censoring weight 1.      reproduces analysis code function ported .      adjust censoring, subjects censored early count much      subjects followed end.    * `"ipcw"`: one row per subject, scored      `Surv(last stop, status last stop)` weighted inverse      probability censoring (Graf et al., 1999). Subjects still risk      \(t\) get weight \(1/G(t)\); subjects event      \(T_i \le t\) get \(1/G(T_i^-)\). \(G\) Kaplan-Meier      censoring distribution analysis-set subjects, floored 0.001. two settings give different numbers compared ; compare `alpha`/`lambda` within one setting.
